headline: Pricing and cost discipline drive record margins
summary_short: Second-quarter net sales rose 6.3% year-over-year to $671.1 million, with operating margin expanding 300 basis points to 25.2% and diluted EPS up 25.1% to $3.09. The company raised its 2026 share repurchase authorization by $50 million and updated full-year guidance.
summary_long: Net sales grew 6.3% y/y to $671.1M, led by North America pricing (+6.0%) and Europe volume/price/FX gains (+7.6%, a record 13.7% operating margin). Gross margin expanded 100bp to 47.4% on lower material costs and cost savings; operating margin rose 300bp to 25.2%, aided by a $5.5M eminent domain settlement. Net income rose 22.7% to $127.0M; diluted EPS rose 25.1% to $3.09 on the net income gain plus a 1.8% y/y buyback-driven share-count reduction. Operating cash flow rose $89.8M y/y to $215.0M; cash ended at $450.5M. Board raised the buyback authorization to $200.0M and declared a $0.30/share dividend. FY2026 outlook updated: operating margin 19.7%-20.5% (includes a $10.0M-$12.0M land-sale gain), tax rate 25.0%-26.0%, capex $80.0M-$90.0M.

drivers.explanation: Management frames the quarter as solid execution across operations, with pricing actions, European volume growth, and cost-savings initiatives driving margin expansion alongside a one-time eminent domain settlement gain.

North America growth (+6.0%) driven by 2025 tariff-related pricing actions, partly offset by lower unit volumes on a softer market; Europe growth (+7.6%) from higher unit volumes, price increases, and ~$3.7M favorable FX.
Margin expanded 100bp to 47.4% on lower material costs as a percentage of sales and cost-savings initiatives; North America margin rose to 50.2% from 49.5%, Europe to 38.2% from 36.2%.
Margin rose 300bp to 25.2%, including a 100bp benefit from a $5.5M eminent domain settlement plus 2025 strategic cost-savings initiatives and higher gross profit.
Diluted EPS growth (25.1%) exceeded net income growth (22.7%) on a 1.8% y/y reduction in weighted diluted shares from the quarter's $48.7M buyback.
Operating cash flow rose $89.8M y/y to $215.0M on higher net income and working-capital changes; investing outflows fell $31.9M y/y to $8.6M on lower capital expenditures.
Not explained in the release; no debt-repayment or refinancing narrative is given for the y/y decline.
